prompt: What is a landing zone, in the Cloud Adoption Framework's sense?
hint: Think of a plot of land.

choices.text: A template for a virtual machine with hardened settings
choices.why: That is one resource. A landing zone is the governed place resources go into.

choices.text: A subscription that arrives already governed
choices.why: Right. Placed, with policies, budget, network and roles, before the first deployment.

choices.text: A region Microsoft reserves for new customers
choices.why: Regions have nothing to do with it.

choices.text: A button in the portal that creates a subscription
choices.why: It is a design, not a product or a button.

prompt: Which of these belongs to the platform landing zone rather than to a workload landing zone?
hint: Built once, for everybody.

choices.text: The shop's web app
choices.why: That is a workload, in its own landing zone.

choices.text: The `shop-staging` subscription
choices.why: That is one of the shop's workload landing zones.

choices.text: The hub network connected to the office
choices.why: Right. Every workload uses it; the platform team builds it once.

choices.text: The orders database of production
choices.why: That belongs to the workload that owns the orders.

prompt: How many design areas does the Cloud Adoption Framework list for a platform landing zone?
hint: Count the rows of the table.

prompt: Somebody creates a subscription by hand, outside the vending process, in a tenant with no default management group set. Where does it land?
hint: Lesson 2 named the top of the tree.

choices.text: In the sandbox group
choices.why: Only if somebody set sandbox as the default.

choices.text: Beside the creator's other subscriptions
choices.why: Placement is not decided by who created it.

choices.text: Nowhere until a management group is chosen
choices.why: Every subscription has a parent from the start.

choices.text: Under the tenant root group
choices.why: Right. Governed by almost nothing, until moved.

prompt: The shop's platform team is tempted to skip subscription vending and let each team create subscriptions as needed, moving them afterwards. What does the lesson say goes wrong?
hint: What governs a subscription between its creation and its move?

choices.text: Until someone remembers to move it, it sits nearly ungoverned
choices.why: Right. Vending makes the subscription arrive placed, budgeted and connected.

choices.text: Each team would be billed in a different currency
choices.why: Currency is not decided by who creates the subscription.

choices.text: Subscriptions created by teams cannot be moved at all
choices.why: They can be moved; the problem is the time before.

choices.text: Teams would need Global Administrator to do it
choices.why: Creating a subscription is a billing permission, not that directory role.

prompt: Issuing a new subscription on request, already placed and governed, is what CAF calls subscription ___.
hint: Like a machine that hands out a product.

prompt: Why does CAF advise against management groups for production, testing and development?
hint: What is a test environment for?

choices.text: Staging should be governed exactly like production
choices.why: Right. Different policies would make the test measure something else.

choices.text: Management groups cannot hold more than one subscription
choices.why: They can hold many.

choices.text: Environments are separated by region instead
choices.why: They are separated by subscription.

choices.text: Development environments must not be governed at all
choices.why: They are governed; sandbox has lighter rules, not none.

prompt: Match each of the shop's subscriptions, or needs, to its management group in the CAF tree.
hint: The shop serves the internet.

prompt: What is the intermediate root management group for?
hint: It sits directly under the tenant root.

choices.text: To hold the platform team's own subscriptions
choices.why: Those go under platform, one level further down.

choices.text: So nothing has to be assigned at the tenant root itself
choices.why: Right. Everything of the organisation's hangs under one group it owns.

choices.text: To double the depth limit from six to twelve
choices.why: The limit is six whatever the groups are called.

choices.text: To separate the tenant into two directories
choices.why: A management group never splits a directory.

prompt: Without `@batchSize(1)`, `alz.bicep` still compiled. What could go wrong when it was deployed?
hint: Copy loops run in parallel by default.

choices.text: Nothing: Bicep added the dependencies between items itself
choices.why: It cannot see that one item's parent is another item's name.

choices.text: The groups would be created in a random region
choices.why: Management groups have no region.

choices.text: A child might be created before its parent existed, and fail
choices.why: Right. Serial, in list order, puts every parent first.

choices.text: Resource Manager would refuse the template as malformed
choices.why: The template is valid either way; the problem is timing.

prompt: CAF advises against giving workload teams roles at management group scope. Why?
hint: A permission reaches down.

choices.text: Roles cannot be assigned on management groups
choices.why: They can; platform teams use that.

choices.text: It costs more than a role on a subscription
choices.why: Role assignments are not billed.

choices.text: Management group roles expire after a day
choices.why: Nothing like that applies to them.

choices.text: It reaches every subscription below, including other teams'
choices.why: Right. Give it at their subscriptions and groups instead.

prompt: On what date does Azure Blueprints stop working altogether, by Microsoft's retirement page?
hint: The last row of the timeline.

choices.text: 31 July 2026
choices.why: That is when new definitions stopped.

choices.text: 31 January 2027
choices.why: Right. The API, the commands and the portal pages go.

choices.text: 31 October 2026
choices.why: That is when new assignments stop.

choices.text: 11 July 2026, the original date
choices.why: That date was extended.

prompt: Blueprints did two jobs. Which feature takes over storing and versioning the definition?
hint: The other takes over assigning and locking.

choices.text: Management groups
choices.why: They hold subscriptions, not templates.

choices.text: Azure Policy initiatives
choices.why: An initiative groups policy definitions; it does not store templates.

choices.text: Template specs, or a Git repository
choices.why: Right. Deployment stacks take the other job.

choices.text: Resource locks
choices.why: A lock protects; it stores nothing.

prompt: A resource is removed from a stack's template and the stack is updated with `--action-on-unmanage detachAll`. What happens to the resource?
hint: Detach is the cautious one.

choices.text: It stays in Azure, no longer managed
choices.why: Right. A mistake in the template leaves a resource, not a hole.

choices.text: It is deleted
choices.why: That is `deleteResources` or `deleteAll`.

choices.text: The update is refused until it is deleted by hand
choices.why: The update goes ahead.

choices.text: It is moved to the decommissioned group
choices.why: Stacks do not move resources between groups.

prompt: A stack manages the shop's firewall with `--deny-settings-mode denyDelete`. ana, an Owner of the subscription, tries to delete the firewall and is not an excluded principal. What happens?
hint: A deny assignment overrides role assignments.

choices.text: It is deleted, because Owner may do anything
choices.why: A deny assignment beats any role assignment.

choices.text: It is deleted, and the stack recreates it at the next update
choices.why: It is never deleted: the request is refused.

choices.text: The delete waits for approval by the stack's owner
choices.why: Deny settings refuse; they do not queue requests.

choices.text: The delete is refused
choices.why: Right. Only the principals named in the exclusion list get through.

prompt: At which scopes can a deployment stack be created? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three of lesson 2's four boxes.

choices.text: A resource group
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A subscription
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A management group
choices.why: Right. It can manage lesson 4's policy assignments there.

choices.text: The tenant
choices.why: No stacks at the tenant, so the management group tree is deployed the ordinary way.

prompt: A deployment stack can protect what it manages with a ___ assignment, which refuses deleting it even to an Owner.
hint: The opposite of allow.

prompt: Put the steps of giving the shop a governed platform in a sensible order, by the lesson.
hint: The tree before the rules, the rules before the workloads.
items: deploy the management group tree under an intermediate root
assign the policies to the tree's groups
set a default management group for new subscriptions
trap: Vending comes last: it places subscriptions into a tree that already has its rules.

prompt: An old internal wiki tells new teams to start their landing zone from a blueprint. What should the platform team do with it now?
hint: What does Blueprints accept after October 2026?

choices.text: Rewrite it around template specs and deployment stacks
choices.why: Right. The two features Microsoft names as the replacement.

choices.text: Keep it, since existing blueprints still work until 2027
choices.why: New assignments stop on 31 October 2026, so a new team cannot follow it.

choices.text: Replace Blueprints with Azure Policy initiatives alone
choices.why: Policy covers the rules, not the lifecycle and locking of resources.

choices.text: Point it at the portal's Blueprints page instead
choices.why: The page goes with the service in January 2027.

prompt: The shop keeps lesson 2's tree, with `mg-shop-prod` and `mg-shop-nonprod`, and a staging deploy passes but the same release is denied in production by a policy staging lacks. What does CAF's reasoning say?
hint: What was the test supposed to measure?

choices.text: Add the policy to staging by hand each time it fails
choices.why: That keeps two trees in step by memory, which is what fails.

choices.text: Move production under `mg-shop-nonprod` to make them equal
choices.why: That loosens production instead of tightening staging.

choices.text: Put both subscriptions under one group so they share every rule
choices.why: Right. Environments by subscription, governance by group.

choices.text: Remove the policy from production
choices.why: The policy may be right; the tree is the defect.
